item.title: Bridging Alloy and OpenTelemetry: the OTel engine is now in Public Preview (8 minute read)
item.description: Grafana Alloy's OpenTelemetry engine is now in Public Preview as of Alloy v1.21.0. It runs standard OpenTelemetry Collector YAML configuration and supports Fleet Management for remote configuration. Users can run the OTel engine alongside the default engine or switch between them using an environment variable.

item.title: Lakebase Postgres is now generally available on Google Cloud (11 minute read)
item.description: Lakebase Postgres is now generally available on Google Cloud as a fully managed, serverless database. It includes autoscaling, scale to zero, instant branching, and point-in-time recovery to help teams build and ship faster without managing database infrastructure. Operational and analytical data share the same storage format.

item.title: Shopify Overexposed Scans GKE Ingresses and Cloud Run for Exposure (4 minute read)
item.description: Shopify Overexposed is an internal scanner that finds GKE Ingresses and Cloud Run services reachable without authentication. A rebuild on GCP Cloud Asset Inventory plus an anonymous HTTP probe cut inconclusive Ingress verdicts by about 80%.

item.title: The hidden latency inside your database (8 minute read)
item.description: PlanetScale Metal uses locally attached NVMe storage to eliminate network latency between compute and disk. This architecture avoids the IOPS limits of network-attached storage like EBS, where defaults are often capped at 3,000 IOPS. Benchmarks show an instance with local NVMe storage costs $551.15 per month compared to $1,513.82 for a comparable EBS setup.

item.title: Deep dive: Auto scaling response times on Amazon ECS (12 minute read)
item.description: Amazon ECS now offers high-resolution CPU and memory metrics published every 20 seconds for target tracking, allowing services to detect and respond to load changes faster than the default 60-second resolution. AWS benchmarks show time to trigger scale-out fell 76%, from 363 seconds to 86 seconds, and SLA breach time on Fargate decreased 69% in gradual ramp tests.

item.title: Floci (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Floci is a free, open-source local AWS emulator for development, testing, and CI that works without a cloud account or auth token. It supports standard tools like Terraform and the AWS CLI, and Lambda or RDS workloads run in real Docker containers for higher fidelity than mocks. The project also acts as a drop-in replacement for LocalStack.

item.title: Agent-Desktop (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Agent-Desktop is a CLI that enables AI agents to see and operate desktop applications on macOS, Windows, and Linux through the OS accessibility tree. It reads the accessibility tree as JSON, allowing agents to interact with elements without using screenshots or pixel matching.

item.title: Optimize your NRQL with Macros! (2 minute read)
item.description: New Relic introduced NRQL Macros, which save an expression as a reusable named shortcut called by prefixing the name with a dollar sign. Macros can simplify long WHERE clauses and update many dashboard widgets by changing one definition.

item.title: Detect when your AI agent copies a self-replicating prompt injection (11 minute read)
item.description: Datadog tested its AI Guard product against self-replicating prompt injections that OpenAI reported in September. AI Guard flagged a planted email as indirect prompt injection at 99.5% confidence and a planted CSV file as jailbreak and obfuscation.

item.description: Ads get ignored on social media but not in TLDR! Reach DevOps and platform engineers where they actually pay attention. Learn more about sponsorship opportunities.

item.title: The boundary problem in agentic AI is a platform problem (11 minute read)
item.description: Agentic AI risk comes from tool permissions that accumulate unnoticed, so boundaries belong in the platform.

item.description: The CNCF End User Technical Advisory Board will preview KubeCon North America 2026 in Salt Lake City on November 9 to 12.

item.title: pull_request_target blocked by default December 2 (2 minute read)
item.description: GitHub Actions will block pull_request_target events by default in all public repositories starting December 2.

item.title: Cloudflare Services for Private Origins Is Now Generally Available (5 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare can now route public requests to private origin IPs over existing Cloudflare One connectivity while applying WAF, caching, bot management, and Workers. Origins retain private addresses without inbound firewall exceptions. Setup requires account enablement, supported connectivity, and appropriate return routes.

item.title: Spacelift Brought Scale to Your IaC Provisioning. Now We're Automating Everything That Happens After. (4 minute read)
item.description: Spacelift is expanding from IaC provisioning into Day 2 operations with Spacelift Flows. It also renamed its IaC and GitOps offering to 'Spacelift Deploy' and bundles it with the Spacelift Intelligence assistant in one control plane.

item.title: Grafana 13.3 release: manage variables across dashboards, share findings with Notebooks, a UI refresh, and more (6 minute read)
item.description: Grafana 13.3 adds cross-dashboard variables and Notebooks, both in public preview, plus the first phase of a visual refresh. It also brings Assistant dashboard plans and a generally available Undo turn option for reverting Assistant edits.

item.title: How to troubleshoot GKE workloads faster with VPC Flow Logs (5 minute read)
item.description: Google Cloud shows how GKE metadata in VPC Flow Logs gives workload-level attribution for network traffic without agents or sidecars. It walks through three Flow Analyzer examples on the Online Boutique demo.

item.title: Default to serverless for AI agents, then let production data decide what moves (10 minute read)
item.description: Datadog argues that serverless should be the first execution model teams evaluate for AI agents. It cites a study of over 35,000 coding agent sessions where LLM or tool calls filled only 20% of the median session.

item.title: What's actually running under your EC2 instance? (Sponsor)
item.description: Meet the AWS Nitro System, the foundation for Amazon EC2 instances. Its purpose-built Nitro Cards handle networking, storage and management, delivering stronger security and faster performance while all of the host's CPU and memory go to your instance. Check out the deep dive

item.title: Vorssaint (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Vorssaint is a free and open-source macOS menu bar toolkit that replaces dozens of paid utility apps. It offers per-app volume controls, window snapping, a clipboard history, and system monitors. The tool runs locally with no account, telemetry, or subscription required.

item.title: OpenMAIC (GitHub Repo)
item.description: OpenMAIC is an open-source AI platform that transforms documents into interactive classroom experiences with AI teachers, slides, and simulations. It supports over 20 providers, including OpenAI, Anthropic, and local options like Ollama.

item.title: How GKE networking scales to support high densities of concurrent AI agents (4 minute read)
item.description: Google Cloud explains how GKE Dataplane V2 avoids Cilium's 65,536 identity limit for high-density agent workloads by moving high-cardinality pod labels to annotations. The post reports 300 sandboxes per second at sub-second latency.

item.title: Do the math: How we took over ChatGPT accounts (10 minute read)
item.description: Researchers found a vulnerability that allowed them to take over ChatGPT accounts just by sending a victim a link. The exploit chain combined a MathLive keyboard feature and the HTML Preview to bypass the sandbox, allowing malicious code to run as chatgpt.com and access private conversations. OpenAI fixed the issue on October 26 and classified the report as P1.

item.title: Trace voice agents with Datadog Agent Observability (5 minute read)
item.description: Datadog Agent Observability now captures audio, transcripts, token usage, and tool calls for voice agents built on the OpenAI Realtime API. It also adds tracing for Amazon Nova 2 Sonic, with ElevenLabs Realtime support planned for ddtrace 4.17.0.

item.title: Free, 24-hour dev conference + keynote with Andrew Ng — November 12 (Sponsor)
item.description: Explore agent memory, MCP, evals, security, and production AI across 100+ technical sessions at Neo4j NODES 2026. Register free.

item.title: OpenTelemetry eBPF Instrumentation reaches v1.0.0 (19 minute read)
item.description: The release marks general availability for the project's kernel-level observability tool.

item.title: TCP Use-After-Free: CVE-2026-98432/CVSS 9.8 (12 minute read)
item.description: CVE-2026-98432 is a CVSS 9.8 remote use-after-free in Linux's IPv4 TCP handshake, fixed in upstream stable kernels on October 15.

item.title: Match monitoring depth to workload needs with Infrastructure Basic (4 minute read)
item.description: Datadog describes Infrastructure Basic, a lightweight tier that collects core host metrics and selected process status for lower-priority workloads. It uses the same Agent in basic mode and can run alongside Pro or Enterprise tiers in one organization.

item.title: Supabase Compute: run your agents inside your project (3 minute read)
item.description: Supabase launched Supabase Compute in private alpha to run agents, background jobs, and APIs directly alongside user data. The offering currently supports the us-west-2 region. Dreambase reported query latency dropped from 65 ms in another region to a median of 2.9 ms after moving a data agent to the new platform.

item.title: Announcing the Workload Conformance Working Group (4 minute read)
item.description: The Kubernetes community launched a Workload Conformance Working Group to write a shared specification and tests for how workloads behave at runtime. The group aims for a stable first specification within two to three release cycles and seeks input from operators and application maintainers.

item.title: One Hub, 34 Clusters: Lessons From a GitOps Control Plane at Scale (5 minute read)
item.description: Nitish Mane describes an Argo CD hub that managed 34 clusters across 22 AWS accounts and one Oracle Cloud tenancy from a repository of 174 Helm charts. Per-cluster contracts, CI manifest diffs, and no-prune settings kept changes safe, and onboarding reportedly fell from 4 days to 1.7 hours.

item.title: How to Integrate Terraform with Backstage for Self-Service (17 minute read)
item.description: Mattias Fjellström explains how to connect Terraform with Backstage through the software catalog, software templates that open pull requests, and the Spacelift plugin. Backstage collects requests but does not run Terraform, so version control remains the source of truth.

item.title: 1M Durable Workflows per Second on Postgres (6 minute read)
item.description: DBOS scaled a benchmark of no-op durable workflows from 20,000 per second on one Postgres server to one million across 50 shards using PgDog. The main obstacle was a contention feedback loop that collapsed throughput when a shard slowed down. Advisory locks limited concurrent dequeuers and restored stable scaling.

item.title: Macro (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Macro is a unified workspace that combines email, chat, docs, tasks, agents, and CRM into a single interface with shared team memory. It links all objects, such as emails and tasks, via a bidirectional graph so AI agents and users can search across tools without switching contexts.

item.title: DeepTutor (GitHub Repo)
item.description: DeepTutor provides lifelong personalized tutoring with features like folder-based learning workspaces, daily practice, and persistent usage accounting. The open source platform includes over 100 CLI apps the tutor can run, supports OpenAI Codex OAuth for sign-in, and offers MCP Services stores on a per-account basis.

item.title: The AI observability race will be won on interoperability (5 minute read)
item.description: OpenTelemetry offers a common method to capture and describe AI behavior using shared conventions for conversations and messages. This standardization helps teams compare models, reduce duplicate integration work, and measure cost per outcome rather than just token counts.

item.title: The Pwn Request Reckoning: What Still Works Against GitHub Actions (9 minute read)
item.description: GitHub's upcoming platform changes in 2026 will make pull_request_target attacks harder, but gaps remain involving outdated checkout versions, script injection, and unprotected triggers like issue_comment. Pinning actions to old SHA values predating the July 2026 backport release bypasses the new checkout protections entirely. The default policy also does not apply to private repositories or workflow_run events.

item.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows generally available (3 minute read)
item.description: GitHub Agentic Workflows automates reasoning-based tasks like issue triage and CI failure analysis using coding agents inside GitHub Actions.

item.title: One pod, one node: The architecture behind serverless Kubernetes on AWS (8 minute read)
item.description: AWS Fargate for EKS routes pods with an admission webhook, provisions a dedicated environment per pod through its own scheduler, and attaches each pod to the customer VPC through a dedicated network interface.

item.title: Gheist: Attempted Scaled Abuse of Stolen GitHub Tokens Stumbles (9 minute read)
item.description: Gheist is an automated campaign that plants secret-dumping workflows in repositories using stolen GitHub tokens. It has targeted over 850 compromised accounts since September 15. GitHub's recent security controls blocked the attack in public repositories, but private and enterprise environments remain vulnerable.

item.title: What Took the Internet Offline in Q3 2026 (8 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare Radar recorded 49 Internet disruptions during the third quarter, including 19 government-directed shutdowns and 14 power outages. The incidents illustrate dependencies beyond network redundancy.

item.title: How to Build Golden Paths in Platform Engineering (19 minute read)
item.description: Spacelift defines a golden path as an opinionated, documented, self-service route for a common task. The guide lists five building blocks and four rollout phases, with a worked Postgres example on AWS built as an rds-postgres module using OpenTofu 1.10.3. Production gets Multi-AZ and deletion protection.

item.title: Why Kubernetes autoscalers keep fighting each other (and why the solution must be autonomous) (7 minute read)
item.description: Nikhil Kurup argues that HPA, VPA, KEDA, and Karpenter mutate the same workload fields from independent loops, producing four failure modes, including a VPA and HPA death spiral and GitOps drift ping-pong. He calls for a unified, predictive autoscaler with explainable decisions.

item.title: The Bridge to Agent-Scale Git Infrastructure (8 minute read)
item.description: GitHub is replacing repository-wide write serialization with per-reference quorums to overcome cross-region latency during its Azure migration. Internal tests showed 3–4x higher throughput for writes to different references, while an object-storage-backed design allows read capacity to scale independently.

item.title: How do you respond when your AI tooling and models fail? (Sponsor)
item.description: Engineers from incident.io and Skyscanner discuss what happens when AI tooling becomes a single point of failure, and what both teams are doing about it. Watch Now→

item.title: Agent-Reach (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Agent-Reach is an open source CLI tool that lets agents read and search platforms like Twitter, Reddit, YouTube, GitHub, and Bilibili without API fees. It handles login-gated sites, video content, and Chinese platforms to provide structured data for AI agents.

item.title: OpenBot (GitHub Repo)
item.description: OpenBot is a local-first desktop workspace for persistent AI teammates that runs Codex, Claude, Grok, and Gemini with dedicated workspaces and task queues. It provides a shared desktop channel, file transfers, and an embedded browser that agents can control. A development preview is available for macOS, Windows, and Linux.

item.title: Before you expand your GPU pool, measure the outcome (8 minute read)
item.description: Teams should define each workload's outcome and deadline before expanding a GPU pool. Teams can stagger flexible jobs, load test sustainable serving capacity, and track cost per verified outcome with OpenCost before adding GPUs.

item.title: Fixing Tool-Call Accuracy in vLLM (7 minute read)
item.description: vLLM 0.31 can achieve 100% tool-call schema accuracy for Kimi and DeepSeek models through constrained decoding, a technique that guarantees schema adherence during token generation. This fixes a reliability issue where vLLM 0.28 produced invalid tool calls 8% of the time, causing agentic workloads to build up nonsensical context.

item.title: Scope Your Personal Access Tokens (6 minute read)
item.description: Supabase personal access tokens can be restricted to specific organizations, projects, permissions, and expiration dates for CI pipelines and other integrations.

item.title: PyTorch Conference 2026: Google and Meta Open-Source TorchTPU for Native PyTorch on TPUs (4 minute read)
item.description: Google and Meta open-sourced TorchTPU, a native PyTorch backend for Google's TPUs, at PyTorch Conference North America 2026.

item.description: AWS engineers compare two observability patterns for AI agents on Amazon EKS.
